source: Mandel, Karvetski, Dhami (2018) Boosting intelligence analysts judgment accuracy
finding: Real UK intelligence analysts trained in ACH and told to use it were not more accurate than untrained analysts on a probability task. Controls were slightly better.
numbers: N=50 analysts, 25 per group. Mean absolute error: control 0.21, ACH 0.26, d=0.43, p=.14 (not significant, favors control). Random responding gave MAE 0.33; analysts 0.23, d=0.95.
limits: Single small study, one artificial task (four tribes, 12 cues, truth-serum framing). Low power for group differences.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a named structured method such as ACH improves a judgment. Measure accuracy, not process compliance.

source: Mandel, Karvetski, Dhami (2018) Boosting intelligence analysts judgment accuracy
finding: ACH did help one thing: rating how useful each piece of evidence is. But the ratings did not track accuracy in the ACH group.
numbers: Usefulness-rating accuracy higher in ACH group, d=1.59, p<.001. Correlation of usefulness tracking with accuracy in ACH group r(24)=-.10, p=.63; present in control.
limits: Same N=50. Usefulness measured against a naive Bayes model.
agent_relevance: Evidence scoring (the evidence-file step) can improve while the final judgment does not. Test end answers.

source: Mandel, Karvetski, Dhami (2018) Boosting intelligence analysts judgment accuracy
finding: Analysts probability judgments for four exhaustive hypotheses did not sum to one, and splitting a hypothesis into parts inflated probability (unpacking effect). ACH did not remove this.
numbers: Unpacking factor above 1 in both groups: control d=0.96, ACH M=1.77, d=1.69, both p<.001. Group difference not significant. Mandel and Tetlock later describe ACH analysts as more susceptible to unpacking.
limits: Same N=50.
agent_relevance: Agent hypothesis lists should be checked for coherence (probabilities sum to one, no unpacking inflation) by code, not by prompting.

source: Mandel, Karvetski, Dhami (2018) Boosting intelligence analysts judgment accuracy
finding: Statistical repair beat the method. Forcing judgments to be coherent cut error 35%; averaging across analysts cut it further, 61% in total.
numbers: Coherentized MAE 0.15 vs raw 0.23, d=0.96, p<.001 (35% drop). Coherentized random chance MAE 0.21; analysts better, d=0.64. Gain larger in ACH group (d=1.37) than control (d=0.69). Aggregated plus coherentized: 61% MAE drop.
limits: N=50; the 61% is for aggregated, coherentized judgments from bootstrap groups up to 49.
agent_relevance: For our agent: sample several independent runs, coherentize, aggregate. It is the intervention with measured gains in this field.

source: Mandel, Karvetski, Dhami (2018) Boosting intelligence analysts judgment accuracy
finding: Prior ACH research is thin and mixed. Small samples, no control groups, and few measures of accuracy.
numbers: Cited: Lehner et al. 2008 found ACH reduced confirmation bias in non-analysts but had no effect on analysts. Convertino et al. 2008 had no control group. Kretz et al. 2012 lacked appropriate controls.
limits: Secondary reading of other studies, not re-checked.
agent_relevance: The evidence base for ACH, the best-known evidence-hypothesis matrix step, is weak. Treat it as a hypothesis, not a fact.

source: Mandel and Tetlock (2018) Correcting Judgment Correctives in National Security Intelligence
finding: Core argument: intelligence tradecraft methods were never tested. Heuer defended ACH on common sense and said he would ignore a test that did not replicate how ACH is used.
numbers: Heuer 2010 quote: if testing does not replicate exactly how ACH is used, he would be inclined to ignore it. Cites Mandel et al. 2018.
limits: Perspective piece, hypotheses not new data.
agent_relevance: Be wary of untested sensemaking recipes. Add tests before adding steps to the schema.

source: Mandel and Tetlock (2018) Correcting Judgment Correctives in National Security Intelligence
finding: One-directional warnings against bias (be less overconfident) may just shift the response threshold and create the mirror bias (underconfidence), not better thinking.
numbers: Argument backed by cited work on underconfidence in strategic forecasts. No new numbers.
limits: Hypothesis, partly supported by indirect evidence.
agent_relevance: Debias prompts like avoid overconfidence can overshoot. Check calibration on both sides.

source: Mandel and Tetlock (2018) Correcting Judgment Correctives in National Security Intelligence
finding: Recommends measurement-based correctives: recalibration, aggregation, coherentization, and performance-weighted pooling over narrative tradecraft.
numbers: Cites the 61% error cut in Mandel et al. 2018 as the example.
limits: Advocacy paper.
agent_relevance: Supports a scaffold that ends in a numeric aggregation step.

source: Mandel and Tetlock (2018) Correcting Judgment Correctives in National Security Intelligence
finding: Structured analytic techniques became staple training after the 2004 US reform act, while testing lagged.
numbers: Mandated by the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 per the cited papers.
limits: Context only.
agent_relevance: Adoption is not evidence of effect.

source: Li, Bonepalli, Mohanty (2026) What to Make Sense of in the Era of LLM?
finding: GPT-4 was tested on a 10-document fictional terror plot sensemaking task against a crowd baseline. LLM found more hypotheses but fewer facts.
numbers: Hypotheses covered out of 15: crowd 4 (all comprehensive); GPT-4 holistic 10 (6 comprehensive); step-by-step 3 comprehensive. Facts: crowd 17 (all comprehensive); holistic 6 (0 comprehensive); step-by-step 9 (5 comprehensive).
limits: Preliminary, one dataset, one run per condition, GPT-4 only, answer-key matching by authors.
agent_relevance: Foraging (fact extraction) is the LLM weak step, hypothesis generation the strong one. Forcing steps helps facts, hurts hypotheses.

source: Li, Bonepalli, Mohanty (2026) What to Make Sense of in the Era of LLM?
finding: LLMs merged the Pirolli-Card steps: they pulled facts while selecting documents and jumped to hypotheses during fact extraction.
numbers: Qualitative observation across holistic and step-by-step runs.
limits: Position paper, no statistics.
agent_relevance: Our schema must hold states apart and gate transitions, since the model tends to collapse foraging into synthesis.

source: Li, Bonepalli, Mohanty (2026) What to Make Sense of in the Era of LLM?
finding: Proposed hybrid: humans or a grounded pass do fact gathering, LLM does synthesis. Human analyses captured detail; LLM analyses were abstract.
numbers: Example: an answer-key fact with bank and account details was reduced to has financial ties. Details lost.
limits: Proposal, not tested.
agent_relevance: Add a verbatim-fact ledger before hypothesis generation to stop abstraction drift.

source: Suh, Min, Palani, Xia (2023) Sensecape
finding: Sensecape (LLM tool linking exploration and structuring, built on the foraging/sense loop model) let users explore far more concepts for the same number of prompts.
numbers: Within-subject N=12. Concepts explored: Sensecape M=68.3 (SD 49.1) vs baseline 22.8 (SD 7.7), t(11)=3.1, p=.01. Prompts 7.3 vs 5.8, p=.37. Nodes 26.8 vs 23.5, p=.45.
limits: 12 participants, mean age about 27; baseline was chat plus canvas; self-chosen tasks; not intelligence analysts.
agent_relevance: A hierarchical, revisitable structure raises coverage without more queries. Suggests memory structure beats chat history.

source: Suh, Min, Palani, Xia (2023) Sensecape
finding: Hierarchical structure and revisiting also rose with the tool.
limits: Same N=12. Outcome is activity, not answer quality.
agent_relevance: State as a revisited tree, not a flat log. Revisits are a measurable sign of memory use.

source: Suh, Min, Palani, Xia (2023) Sensecape
finding: Preferences split by goal: tool preferred for deep understanding, plain chat for quick broad answers. Chat judged slightly easier.
numbers: Nine of 12 preferred Sensecape for deeper understanding of a topic; for broad understanding six preferred baseline, one no preference.
limits: Self-report, N=12.
agent_relevance: Heavy structure has a cost. Route easy questions around the full loop.

source: Suh, Min, Palani, Xia (2023) Sensecape
finding: Authors tie the design to the Pirolli-Card two-loop model: structuring information is the move from foraging to sensemaking.
numbers: Design claim in Fig. 2 of the paper.
limits: Uses the model as a design lens, does not test it.
agent_relevance: LLM tools adopt the model as a design frame but no study here tests the model itself.

source: Jhaveri et al. (2026) Failing to Falsify
finding: Eleven LLMs show confirmation bias in a Wason rule-discovery loop: they propose tests that fit their current guess. More bias goes with lower success.
numbers: Success from 6% to 78% across models within 45 turns. Significant positive correlation between incompatible-to-compatible test ratio and success, for both thinking and non-thinking models, stronger for thinking.
limits: Synthetic number-triple task. Correlation across models, not causal alone.
agent_relevance: This is the hypothesis-testing half of the sense loop. A falsification step has a measured basis for LLMs.

source: Jhaveri et al. (2026) Failing to Falsify
finding: Telling the model to think of counterexamples (human-derived interventions) raised rule discovery from 42% to 56% on average.
numbers: Average discovery 42% to 56% across models. Thinking-mode Qwen3-8B: success 0.21, I:C 0.15 baseline; with Think-in-Opposites 0.40, I:C 0.35. Qwen3-32B thinking 0.33 to 0.63 by table reading.
limits: Dual-Goal prompt hurt non-thinking Qwen3-14B (0.23 to 0.13) and 32B (0.33 to 0.10); added tokens per turn in thinking mode. Table column reading approximate.
agent_relevance: Falsification prompts help but are model-dependent. Test per model and watch token cost.

source: Jhaveri et al. (2026) Failing to Falsify
finding: Distilling the intervention behaviour into weights raised success and transferred to a Blicket test.
numbers: Qwen3-8B 0.21 to 0.36 with intervention distillation; Qwen3-32B 0.41 to 0.61; cross-scale plus intervention distillation almost tripled success and more than doubled I:C.
limits: Requires training. Our agent is scaffold-only. Toy task.
agent_relevance: Training route is closed to us; shows the prompt gain is real behaviour change.

source: Marco (2024) Collection-centric information foraging with LLMs
finding: Marco (LLM actions that forage across document collections) made business-document tasks 16% faster with similar accuracy.
numbers: N=16 within-subject. Time 249.6s (SD 88.8) vs 297.3s (SD 89.1). Accuracy Marco 88.1% (SD 10.1) vs baseline 91.9% (SD 8.3), chi2(1)=3.35, p=.067. Seven-minute cap per question.
limits: gpt-3.5-turbo; 16 mostly software staff, mean age 28; accuracy slightly lower, near significance.
agent_relevance: Delegating foraging to an LLM saves time but may cost accuracy. Verify extracted values.

source: Participatory prompting study of GenAI data analysis (2024)
finding: Study of 15 non-expert data workers using Bing Chat mapped benefits to the foraging and sensemaking loops, and barriers to query formulation, context, and verification.
numbers: N=15 (10 men, 5 women), participatory prompting. Qualitative; no counts by design.
limits: Qualitative only, Bing Chat of 2023, non-experts.
agent_relevance: Verification and context passing are the weak points of LLM-assisted foraging.

source: North et al. (2024) Space to Think as a Common Ground for Human-AI Sensemaking
finding: Giving an LLM a human-built space to think (grouped, labeled, annotated notes) improved its sensemaking summaries a lot.
numbers: Score out of 90: docs alone 45.2 (correctness 11.0/30, quality 34.2/60) vs with human space-to-think 68.5 (19.5/30, 49.0/60). Highlights and labeled groups helped further.
limits: Extended abstract; sample size and scoring method not given.
agent_relevance: External structure between raw input and answer carries the gain. Supports a schema state holding a structured shoebox and evidence file.

source: North et al. (2024) Space to Think as a Common Ground for Human-AI Sensemaking
finding: Semantic interaction systems (ForceSpire, StarSpire) that learn what to forage from analyst arrangement sped up sensemaking.
numbers: Reported as accelerated, no numbers in this abstract.
limits: Numbers in cited earlier papers not opened.
agent_relevance: Agent can use its own organization actions as a signal for what to retrieve next.

source: Cheng and Houben (2026) Who's Sense is This?
finding: Workshop position: AI that offers insight early may anchor groups before their own view forms, as in human-human collaborative sensemaking.
numbers: Argument only; no measured effect.
limits: Position paper, three pages, no data.
agent_relevance: Risk for our agent: committing to the first hypothesis early. Delay hypothesis commitment.

source: Maegherman, Ask, Horselenberg, van Koppen (2021) Test of ACH in legal decision-making
finding: ACH training did not cut confirmation bias in a legal task. No confirmation bias appeared in either group.
numbers: N=191 law students randomly assigned to ACH training or general bias information. Each asked 6 of 24 questions. Both groups preferred exonerating questions.
limits: Vignette task, students, floor effect since no bias present; authors say ACH was not applied properly. Read via a summary page, not the full paper.
agent_relevance: Failed test of ACH: low uptake and no gain. Instructions alone may not change behavior.
